key_insight: PercepCap makes video captioning more transparent by explicitly modeling the spatio-temporal evidence behind each description. Instead of jumping straight to a caption, it separates what is seen, where it happens, and when it happens.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of diagnosing spatio-temporal perception errors in video captioning models. Existing MLLMs often produce fluent captions without exposing the underlying perceptual steps, making mistakes hard to detect and fix.
method: Introduces structured spatio-temporal perception for video captioning, separating spatial and temporal evidence before caption generation.
Uses perceptual outputs as intermediate signals so the model can ground descriptions in object locations and event timing.
Improves interpretability by making perception errors visible at the evidence level, not only in the final caption.
impact: This is useful for AI/ML practitioners who need more reliable and debuggable video understanding systems. It can help identify failure modes faster and support better evaluation, training, and trust in multimodal models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing video input -> spatial perception -> temporal perception -> caption output
Annotated video frame timeline highlighting object locations and event moments
Comparison panel: direct captioning vs structured perceptual captioning
Icon set for space/location, time/sequencing, and text generation
paper_title: PercepCap: Video Captioner with Structured Spatio-Temporal Perception
paper_authors: Yifan Xu, Zihao Wang, Zhixiao Wang, Jiaming Zhang, Yichun Yang
